final_candidates.decision_summary: Proline substitution at this conserved aromatic position is predicted to strongly disrupt local backbone geometry and packing. Multiple evidence dimensions converge on severe incompatibility.

Replacing a hydrophobic valine with charged aspartate is expected to disrupt local hydrophobic packing. The substitution is strongly disfavored by evolutionary, sequence-model, and structure-compatibility signals.

This hydrophobic-to-acidic substitution is likely to destabilize the packed central region of PsaE. Its near-zero evolutionary and sequence-model support and poor structural compatibility favor folding disruption.

stop_reason.detail: The current evidence consistently prioritizes these three candidates and additional tools are unlikely to alter their ordering.

history.rationale: Proline substitution at a conserved aromatic position is likely to disrupt local backbone geometry and packing in the folded subunit.

W17P is evolutionarily absent and highly implausible by the PLM, while proline substitution is structurally disfavored. Its structure penalty is substantial but weaker than those of the top three candidates.
Replacing a neighboring aromatic residue with proline may introduce a backbone kink and remove hydrophobic packing, promoting misfolding.

Y18P is absent from the homolog alignment, essentially implausible to the sequence model, and has the most unfavorable ProteinMPNN compatibility among the candidates. These convergent signals make it the strongest folding-disruption candidate.
Introducing a charged aspartate at a hydrophobic position could disrupt a buried core or hydrophobic interface.
V21D is absent from homologs and highly implausible by the PLM, with unfavorable structure compatibility. It remains plausible but is ranked below the more strongly structure-disfavored candidates.
A proline substitution within the central structured region is likely to break secondary structure and destabilize the compact 68-residue fold.
This substitution removes an aromatic packing residue while imposing conformational rigidity in the central region.

Y34P is PLM-incompatible and structurally disfavored, but proline occurs relatively frequently at this position among homologs. The evolutionary tolerance signal lowers its expected disruption relative to other candidates.
A hydrophobic-to-charged substitution at this central valine may be strongly destabilizing if the residue contributes to the protein core.

V36D combines zero observed homolog frequency, essentially zero PLM plausibility, and very poor structure compatibility. It is a strong candidate for destabilizing the hydrophobic core or local packing.
Proline at a central hydrophobic position is expected to perturb backbone structure and weaken fold integrity.

I37P is absent from homologs, nearly impossible under the PLM, and structurally disfavored, supporting folding disruption. It remains a strong backup despite slightly less extreme structural evidence than the top-ranked substitutions.
Aspartate could create an unfavorable buried charge and disrupt hydrophobic packing in the central folded region.

V38D is not observed in homologs, receives a near-zero PLM plausibility score, and is strongly disfavored by the fixed-backbone structure model. The chemically disruptive hydrophobic-to-acidic substitution is therefore retained near the top.
Replacing the aromatic phenylalanine with a charged residue may remove packing interactions and destabilize the adjacent structural segment.
F40D is strongly rejected by the PLM and structure model, consistent with disrupting a hydrophobic site. Its nonzero homolog frequency weakens confidence relative to V36D and V38D.
A proline substitution in the C-terminal structured region could perturb local secondary structure and reduce fold stability.

Although L55P is absent from the sampled homologs, its PLM score is comparatively higher and its structure compatibility is only mildly unfavorable. It is consequently deprioritized as a less reliable folding-disruption choice.
